P19.careNote: Three cactus profiles share one root volume and one watering and weight history. Inspect each cactus, then judge the whole container before watering; a concern with one member is not a separate watering instruction.
P19.name: Shared rehab cactus planter
P19.setupNote: Permanent label #1, formerly A4-B4. Use the current setup and observations in P19's history when assessing this rehabilitation planter.

P20.careNote: The echeveria, two kalanchoes, and elephant bush have separate identity and care profiles but receive water through one shared root volume. Compare all four members and the whole-pot dry-down before watering.
P20.name: Shared succulent planter
P20.setupNote: Square wooden planter with a plastic liner and an owner-drilled approximately one-inch hole through the bottom and liner; outside dimensions remain unmeasured.

P30.careNote: Three visible botanical groups share this container. Judge the shared root volume by full dry-down and whole-pot weight; do not repeatedly wet the pot for one component while the others remain firm.
P30.name: Tiny mixed succulent planter
P30.setupNote: Setup 2, recorded September 3, 2026 for the September 2 care day: 5 inch shallow terra-cotta planter with nursery cacti soil and the owner's top dressing. Exact depth and ingredient proportions remain unrecorded.

P35.careNote: Probable Lithops lesliei and probable Lithops salicola share one container, but may not synchronize their leaf-replacement cycles. Inspect both appearance groups before watering. Keep dry while old leaves are being absorbed; one group's wrinkles alone do not authorize watering the entire pot.
P35.name: Lithops shared planter
P35.setupNote: Repotted September 23, 2026 into the D'vine Dev Blush Mauve pot, setup 2: logged 4.2 in round, with 80% Molly's Succulent Mix and 20% perlite. The seller's selected variant is 4.3 inches. Four visible heads came from two nursery pots; root connections remain unverified.
